title: Ascending degeneracy corrections realize a compatible prefix of faces
statement: Let $G:\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathrm{Ab}$ be a simplicial abelian group with face homomorphisms $d_i$ and degeneracy homomorphisms $s_i$ [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Let $n\geq2$, $0\leq k\leq n$, and $a_i\in G_{n-1}$ for $0\leq i<k$ satisfy $d_i a_j=d_{j-1}a_i$ whenever $0\leq i<j<k$. For any $v\in G_n$, define the finite sequence $v_0,\ldots,v_k\in G_n$ by $v_0=v$ and, for $0\leq r<k$, $$e_r=a_r-d_rv_r,\qquad v_{r+1}=v_r+s_re_r.$$ Then for every $0\leq r\leq k$ one has $d_iv_r=a_i$ for all $0\leq i<r$. Moreover, for each $r<k$, $d_i e_r=0$ and $d_i(s_r e_r)=0$ for all $i<r$, and $d_r(s_r e_r)=e_r$. Thus $v_k$ realizes the entire prescribed prefix; when $k=0$ the sequence consists only of the arbitrary starting element $v$.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, second paragraph (lines 5771-5786): the ascending lower-face correction induction, specialized additively and starting from an arbitrary element.

proof.text: By [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object], the operators are homomorphisms obtained by applying $G$ to the order maps. Contravariance applied to [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-face-identity] gives $d_i d_r=d_{r-1}d_i$ for $i<r$. The needed mixed identities follow directly from the same order maps: $\delta_i(t)=t+\mathbf1_{t\geq i}$ and $\sigma_r(t)=t-\mathbf1_{t>r}$. For $i<r$, both $\sigma_r\delta_i(t)$ and $\delta_i\sigma_{r-1}(t)$ equal $t+\mathbf1_{t\geq i}-\mathbf1_{t\geq r}$, while $\sigma_r\delta_r(t)=t$. Applying $G$ gives $d_i s_r=s_{r-1}d_i$ for $i<r$ and $d_r s_r=1$. These computations prove the instances of Stacks 0167(2),(3) used below.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, ascending correction paragraph; Tag 0167, lemma-relations-face-degeneracy (1)--(3).

proof.text: Use the recursion in the statement and induct on $r\leq k$ with invariant $P(r): d_i v_r=a_i$ for every $i<r$. At $r=0$ there is no such $i$, so $P(0)$ holds for the arbitrary $v_0=v$. For a transition $r<k\leq n$, $r\leq n-1$, so $s_r:G_{n-1}\to G_n$ exists and $e_r=a_r-d_rv_r$ belongs to $G_{n-1}$. All maps are homomorphisms by [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object].

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, ascending correction paragraph; Tag 0167, lemma-relations-face-degeneracy (1)--(3).

proof.text: Assume $P(r)$ and let $i<r$. Compatibility at the pair $(i,r)$ and the face-face identity obtained from [lem-weil-pbc-simplex-face-face-identity] give $$d_i e_r=d_i a_r-d_i d_rv_r=d_{r-1}a_i-d_{r-1}d_iv_r=d_{r-1}(a_i-d_iv_r)=0.$$ Here $i<r<k$, $n\geq2$, and $r\geq1$ whenever this calculation is needed, so both faces with target $G_{n-2}$ are defined. Step 1 and additivity now give $d_i(s_r e_r)=s_{r-1}d_i e_r=0$. Independently, $d_r(s_r e_r)=e_r$ by $d_rs_r=1$, including $r=0$ where the lower-face assertions are empty.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, ascending correction paragraph; Tag 0167, lemma-relations-face-degeneracy (1)--(3).

proof.text: For $i<r$, the preceding calculation gives $d_i v_{r+1}=d_i v_r+d_i(s_r e_r)=a_i$. For $i=r$, it gives $d_r v_{r+1}=d_rv_r+e_r=d_rv_r+(a_r-d_rv_r)=a_r$. Thus $P(r+1)$ holds. Finite induction proves every $P(r)$ for $0\leq r\leq k$ and proves the extra error and correction identities at every transition. Taking $r=k$ gives the required prefix. If $k=0$ there are no transitions, so the sequence is just $v_0=v$.

source.place: Tag 08NZ, lemma-simplicial-group-kan, proof, ascending correction paragraph; Tag 0167, lemma-relations-face-degeneracy (1)--(3).
